description: Bender Wins review, checked 7 Nov 2026: Winible plans from $129.99 a month to $2,999.99 a year, what its winning years claim rests on, and buyer reports.
dek: Bender Wins is Ryan Bender's pick service, sold on Winible from $129.99 a month to $2,999.99 a year. It advertises 7 straight winning years but shows no pick record on its store page. Customer evidence is six CapperTek reviews, three of them from one account.

status.label: Not verified
status.note: Watchdog has not graded a full, time stamped record for Bender Wins. This page reports what we could check and labels everything else.

short_answer: Bender Wins is an active pick service run by Ryan Bender. The store at benderwins.com is a Winible page that lists four paid plans, a football season pass and a free plan, and shows new posts every day, including free picks. Picks are delivered by text or email through Winible.

Whether the picks make money is not shown anywhere we could open. The store claims 7 straight winning years and says a $100 bettor is now betting over $2,150 a unit, but every pick post is locked and we found no public record, outside monitor or contest result.

The customer file is small and split. Former subscribers describe a high volume, systems style service that profits slowly and needs fast betting before lines move, while one reviewer claims the positive reviews are written by Bender himself. Treat the record as unproven.
pricing_intro: Prices below were shown on the Bender Wins Winible store on 7 Nov 2026. Each plan has a monthly and an annual price. Winible says you can unsubscribe anytime, and its refund policy covers all purchases.
pricing: $129.99 a month or $1,299.99 a year. Plays of 1 unit and above, plus a betting guide
Winible: all sales final and non refundable
$149.99 a month or $1,499.99 a year. Full card from 0.25 to 3 units, plus educational videos and the guide
$199.99 a month or $1,999.99 a year. 1 to 4 consensus plays 5 to 7 times a week, plus a tool that triggers plays when 3 or more tracked bettors agree
$299.99 a month or $2,999.99 a year. All of the above
guarantee: There is no performance guarantee. Winible's refund policy, last updated 8 Oct 2026, says all purchases made through Winible are final and non refundable, including for dissatisfaction with the content, and that refunds are offered only at Winible's discretion in limited cases.

The same policy asks buyers to contact Winible support before filing a chargeback, and says a chargeback without doing so may lead to account suspension. We did not see any separate refund promise from Bender Wins.

claims_note: Going from $100 to $2,150 a unit means the bankroll grew more than 21 times, if unit size tracks the bankroll. That is a very large claim to make with no public pick log.
Winning weeks and winning years count periods, not units. A seller can win most weeks and still be close to even if losing weeks are larger.
The quote praising Bender at the top of the store has no name or source attached.
record: What a buyer can check outside the seller: nothing. We found no third party monitor, contest result or regulator record for Bender Wins. A CourtListener search for "benderwins" or "bender wins" returned no case involving the service.

What is the seller's own marketing: the Winible store lists daily posts such as full cards, top plays and consensus plays, but each is locked to subscribers, and the store shows no win and loss record, unit totals or ROI. The winning years claims are not backed by anything we could open. Unit sizes on the full card run from 0.25 to 3 units, which suggests a high volume card with small stakes per play.
Customer reports describe 10 to 20 bets a day and lines that move quickly after release, so a buyer who bets late may get worse prices than any record the seller keeps.

our_data.text: Watchdog grades picks captured from public posts before the game starts. In this edition Bender Wins is not matched to a Watchdog graded record, so we make no claim about how its picks perform.
our_data.context: For scale: Bender Wins advertises winning years rather than a win rate. On the Watchdog board on 7 Nov 2026, {{over60}} of {{established}} established accounts (100 or more graded picks) were at 60% or better, and the median established account won {{median_win}}% of its picks. At standard -110 odds a bettor needs about 52.4% to break even.

customers_intro: Customer evidence on Bender Wins is thin. CapperTek holds six reviews from 2022 to 2026, and three of them come from one account. We found no Trustpilot page, no BBB listing, no reviews on the Winible store and no forum threads. Below is everything we found.

customers.text: A former subscriber on CapperTek said Bender is pretty good but not the best, runs a systems approach with 10 to 20 bets a day, and that lines move fast after release. The reviewer said the service profits slowly, suits people free during work hours with a bankroll of a few thousand dollars, is cheaper on annual or holiday pricing, and would not let people who left rejoin for a while.

A CapperTek reviewer claimed the positive reviews are written by Bender himself, that the picks are mostly favorites and unders, that the free picks have hit barely above 46% over three years, and that he sues people who confront him. We could not confirm any of this and found no such court case.
A CapperTek reviewer called the service legit, but said buyers need to know when plays post and bet quickly, that the volume may be too high for some, and that bankroll growth is slow.

A CapperTek reviewer said they had used Bender for four years without a losing year, and that buyers need accounts at 7 or more sportsbooks to get good prices. The reviewer posted a business email address in the review.
Two older CapperTek reviews praised Bender's daily YouTube videos and free picks (Apr 2022) and said he tries to teach bankroll building rather than just sell picks (Feb 2023).
Three of the six CapperTek reviews, from Feb 2023, Dec 2025 and Oct 2026, were posted by the same account, so the file reflects at most four separate reviewers.

A r/sportsbook thread asked whether Bender Wins is worth paying for. The poster listed $99.99 a month for the Masterclass card and $199.99 a month for the Consensus group or the combined pass, and posted a Masterclass tally for 2025 of 959 wins, 869 losses and 20 pushes, down 66.25 units. That is the poster's count, not ours.
In the same thread a buyer said he felt cheated: the quoted lines of minus 105 were usually not available, bad stretches went quiet, and comments asking for the year to date total were deleted.

A subscriber who said he joined, left and joined again wrote that when he asked for a tracked record he was told to track his own bets. He said he graded the 2026 plays himself and found them down more than 50 units at the quoted odds, and further down at slightly worse odds. He did not post the sheet, and we did not check it.
Another member in the thread said the posted lines are not realistic and the plays are not profitable.

Trustpilot showed no page for benderwins.com, the Better Business Bureau search returned no results for Bender Wins, the Winible store showed no customer reviews, and apart from the r/sportsbook thread above we found no Reddit, TheRX, SBR or Covers forum thread about the service.

conflicts: Winible, the platform that sells the picks, also offers real money games through a partner and ProphetX accounts, according to its refund policy. We saw no sportsbook affiliate link or promo code on the Bender Wins store page itself.
The store grades nothing in public, so any record a subscriber sees comes from the seller.
strengths: Published prices with monthly and annual options and a free plan to sample picks first.
Small stated stakes per play, 0.25 to 3 units, and reviewers describe a focus on bankroll management and straight bets.
Free daily content, including YouTube videos, lets a buyer see the style before paying.
concerns: No public record of any kind. The 7 winning years and $2,150 a unit claims are unsupported.
All Winible sales are final and non refundable.
High volume and fast moving lines mean a buyer may not get the posted prices.
A tiny review file, half from one account, plus an unconfirmed claim that the reviews are written by the seller.
checklist: Ask for every pick from the last 12 months with the line, the odds and the time it was sent. A list of hot runs is not a record.
Count units, not wins. A 60% record at heavy favorites can still lose money.
Read the guarantee for the words refund, credit and extension. Most "guarantees" in this business are credits.
Write down each pick yourself the moment you receive it, with the line you can actually get.
Give any handicapper a few hundred picks before you call them a winner. Short runs swing hard both ways.
faq: It is an active service with a named handicapper, published prices and daily posts on Winible, and former subscribers describe receiving picks as sold. We could not verify any of its performance claims, because it publishes no record.
How much does Bender Wins cost?

On 7 Nov 2026 plans ran from $129.99 a month or $1,299.99 a year for Top Plays up to $299.99 a month or $2,999.99 a year for the Super Pass, plus a $749.95 football season pass and a free plan. Winible says all sales are final.
Does Bender Wins have a verified record?
No. The store claims 7 straight winning years but shows no pick record, we found no outside tracking, and Watchdog has no graded record for it.

For the money you get a high volume card of small unit plays by text or email, plus educational videos on some plans. What is unproven is whether a buyer, betting quickly at the line available at release, beats the roughly 52.4% needed at -110 over time after the subscription cost, and there is no refund if the picks lose.
